fields.questionText:
Jagdish has a field in the shape of a right-angled triangle AQC, right-angled at Q. He wants to leave a space in the form of a square PQRS inside the field for growing wheat and use the remaining part for growing vegetables. Side PQ of the square lies along QC, vertex S lies on the hypotenuse CA, and the square lies on the same side of QC as A. In the field there is a pole marked O on line QC. Taking O as the origin and line QC as the x-axis, the coordinates of P are (–200, 0), of Q are (200, 0), of C are (–600, 0) and of A are (200, 800). Based on the above information, answer the following questions:
(i) PQRS being a square, what are the coordinates of R and S?
(ii) (a) What is the area of square PQRS?
OR
(b) What is the length of diagonal PR of square PQRS?
(iii) If S divides CA in the ratio k : 1, what is the value of k?

rationale: Removed mark/page residues; replaced 'as shown in the figure' with the configuration carried by the row's own steps (C(−600,0), A(200,800), S on CA). Coordinate-geometry content, retagged. Answer unchanged (k=1 verified).

fields.questionText:
A photographer stands on level ground 50 m away from the base of a building. From her position, the angle of elevation of the top of the building is 60°. She also uses a small scale model, a right triangle ABC with base 2 m, height 2√3 m and angle 60° at the base. (Treat the observation point as being at ground level.)
(a) What is the height of the building?
(b) Is the triangle formed by the photographer, the base and the top of the building similar to the model triangle ABC? Why?
(c) She walks straight back, away from the building, until the angle of elevation of the top becomes 30°. How far is she now from the base of the building, and how far did she walk?
fields.answer: (a) 50√3 m (b) Yes, by AA similarity (right angle and 60° angle in both) (c) 150 m from the base; she walked 100 m
solutionSteps: (a) Model: tan 60° = 2√3/2 = √3. For the building, tan 60° = h/50 ⇒ h = 50√3 m. [1 mark]
(b) Both triangles have a right angle and a 60° angle at the base, so they are similar by AA criterion. [1 mark]
(c) Let new distance be d. tan 30° = 50√3/d ⇒ 1/√3 = 50√3/d. [1 mark]
d = 50√3 × √3 = 150 m; distance walked = 150 − 50 = 100 m. [1 mark]
fields.finalAnswer: (a) 50√3 m (b) Yes, AA similarity (c) 150 m from the base; walked 100 m

rationale: Authored row: part (c) needed a non-standard ≈41° angle (LIMIT). Replaced with a 30° elevation part (d=150 m, walked 100 m). Heights & distances content, retagged to trigonometry; steps 1+1+2.
Assertion–Reason on RHS congruence of right triangles is Class 9 congruence content, not in Class 10 2026-27 syllabus; no natural repair within Triangles (similarity/BPT) without a full rewrite.
Tangent ⊥ radius, OA=√(100−64)=6, diameter 12 cm — Circles chapter content; retagged. Answer correct.
Triangle-inequality / construction feasibility is Class 7/9 content with no home in the 2026-27 Class 10 syllabus; preboard row, not authored.
Median via midpoint + distance formula is Coordinate Geometry. E(1,3/2), BE=√(125/4)=5√5/2 verified.

fields.questionText: A circle is inscribed in a right-angled triangle ABC, right-angled at B. If BC = 7 cm and AB = 24 cm, find the radius of the circle.
solutionSteps: [1 mark] AC = √(24² + 7²) = √625 = 25 cm. Let the radius be r cm.
[1 mark] Tangents from B are equal and the radii to the points of contact on AB and BC form a square with B, so the tangent lengths from B are r; tangent lengths from A = 24 − r and from C = 7 − r.

rationale: Incircle radius via tangent lengths is Circles content; retagged. Garbled steps ('√242 + 72', '1 2 ×') rewritten cleanly; r = 3 cm verified. Stem typo 'rightangled' fixed.
Ladder at 60°, h = 13 sin 60° = 13√3/2 m — heights & distances, retagged to trigonometry; single-ratio item is Easy. Answer correct.

fields.questionText:
A teacher sets up a geometry problem: In △ABC, points D and E are marked on sides AB and AC respectively. It is given that DE ∥ BC. The teacher asks students to find relationships between the segments.
(i) If AD = 2 cm, DB = 3 cm and AE = 1.5 cm, find EC.
(ii) Are △ADE and △ABC similar? Justify using an appropriate criterion.
(iii) If, further, BC = 5 cm, find the length of DE.
fields.answer: (i) 2.25 cm (ii) Yes, by AA criterion (corresponding angles equal) (iii) DE = 2 cm
solutionSteps: (i) Since DE ∥ BC, by BPT: AD/DB = AE/EC ⇒ 2/3 = 1.5/EC ⇒ EC = 4.5/2 = 2.25 cm. [1 mark]
(ii) DE ∥ BC ⇒ ∠ADE = ∠ABC and ∠AED = ∠ACB (corresponding angles); hence △ADE ~ △ABC by AA criterion. [1 mark]
(iii) AB = AD + DB = 5 cm; from △ADE ~ △ABC, DE/BC = AD/AB = 2/5. [1 mark]
fields.finalAnswer: (i) 2.25 cm (ii) Yes, by AA criterion (iii) DE = 2 cm

rationale: Authored 4-mark case had only two parts; added part (iii) (DE = 2 cm via similarity) to give a 1+1+2 case structure. Existing answers verified.
